messages.author: 8df77a1c1b1da14e
messages.subject: specifying inits in runMCMC
parts:
Too many posts from me in the last few days, but one more question.

Has there been a change recently in how the function runMCMC uses provided initial values?
If I compile and run a model once, then use Cnim$setData(NewData) to insert new data into the model, it appears that "runMCMC" does not actually use the inits that are provided in the call to that function. It generates warnings about certain nodes where logProb is -Inf. 
Take a simple site occupancy model as an example:

model <- nimbleCode({
    psi ~ dunif(0,1)
    p ~ dunif(0,1)
    for(i in 1:ncells){
        z[i] ~ dbern(psi)
        pz[i] <- p*z[i]
        y[i]~dbin(pz[i],noccs)
    }
})

What seems to be happening is that instead of using the inits for z provided to runMCMC to fit the second data set, it uses as inits the final values in the model from the previous model fitting (the documentation says this is the case if inits are not provided to runMCMC).The result is that in some cases z[i]==0 and y[i]>0, which is logically not possible. In JAGS this generates a message about "nodes inconsistent with parents".
I attached a simple example that demonstrated the issue.

Two other things to note:
1. In JAGS this situation crashes JAGS, but in NIMBLE it seems to move past the inconsistency, find the right values for z, and produce results that seem reasonable. So maybe it isn't cause for concern.
2. I don't remember this happening previously. Yesterday I (needlessly) ran the code suggested in Perry's post from yesterday, so I wonder if that could be relevant. I don't think so, because I tried my script on another computer with NIMBLE 0.7.0, and the behavior was the same. My version of NIMBLE is 0.7.1, and R is 3.4.3.

Any thoughts?

Thanks,
Glenn Stauffer

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: specifying inits in runMCMC
parts:
Glenn, I'm sorry for the short delay on this, but it took us a while to track down exactly what was going on here.  For better or for worse, this had nothing to do with the MCMC, nor with the runMCMC function and it's handling of initial values which are provided as an argument.

Your example brought to light yet another "corner case" in terms of model initialization, the process in which nimble "inspects" model objects to make sure they are "fully initialized" -- that is, all nodes contain valid values, which are consistent with the rest of the model, and all model log-densities have been calculated and reflect the current values of stochastic nodes in the model.

Anyway, your example gave rise to a situation where intermediate deterministic nodes in the model (in your case, the pz[i]) were not having their values updated in the correct (topological) order, during the course of model initialization.  Thus, nimble was reporting that the values of the stochastic dependents (y[i]) were invalid, as a result of the "parent" deterministic probability nodes (pz[i]) not being calculated at the correct time.... if that makes sense.

The final thing I should say, is that this "model initialization" routine takes place at the beginning of every call to runMCMC(), that is, before the MCMC begins operating.

We've fixed this problem in the development branch of nimble.  The fix will be included in our next major/minor release, but until then, you can install the development version directly from GitHub, using:

devtools::install_github("nimble-dev/nimble", ref = "devel", subdir = "packages/nimble")

Please give it a go, and let us know if this clears up your problem.

And make sure to keep in touch with any further questions or problems that you have.

Cheers!
Daniel
for the NIMBLE development team

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: specifying inits in runMCMC
parts:
We should also add that in Glenn's case (as would also be the case in
all but some very unusual situations) while the model initialization
reported something unusual,
by the end of the model initialization, everything was as it should
be. That is why Glenn's MCMC ran fine despite the warning - the
initialization
ended up with the correct initial values before the MCMC started,
despite temporarily doing some calculations with incorrect initial
values.

So, Glenn, you should see that if you run the code off the development
version the warning will disappear but the MCMC output should be
identical
to what you have already gotten.

And even in the unusual corner cases where the model initialization
was done "incorrectly", the MCMC output would still be valid, albeit
from
different starting values than planned.

Chris

messages.author: 8df77a1c1b1da14e
messages.subject: Re: specifying inits in runMCMC
parts:
I think that all makes sense, how if the pz[i] nodes are calculated at the wrong time, then there are inconsistencies with the y[i] nodes. I suspected that the MCMC was working OK despite the warnings, so it is reassuring to know that it is so. In any case I installed the development branch, and tried it out with my toy example. Indeed, the warnings are gone, and all looks OK now.

Thanks,
Glenn
